timecoded_text_to_speech.text: Aspen, Colorado has produced a lot of famous athletes and one of them certainly is Andy
Mill, a longtime member of the US ski team, a great finish in the 1976 in Brook Downhill
under adverse conditions I may say.
So we're here to honor Dr. Richard Steppen.
What does that name mean to you in your life and as a friend, as a doctor, as an inspiration?
Well, I think for a lot of us, he not only fixed our bodies, but he really touched our
hearts.
So when you have something in your life where you know if you do get hurt, there's only,
there's anything good about getting hurt is having knowing that he is in your life.
And when you are in his presence, you know you're going to be in great care, not only, you
know, as a surgeon, but as a great friend.
And a lot of times we were inspired to come back, not only because of our own hearts and
our own passions, but because of him and his efforts in trying to help you get back.
So he inspired us so much that a lot of times we wanted to do it for him as much as we
wanted to do it for ourselves.
Did he make a difference in your life besides fixing you?
Would your life have been the same if you hadn't had Dr. Steppen in it?
Yeah, it would have probably been the same, but I think that he just was really a profound
figure in the back of our minds.
I mean, I didn't live in South Lake Thailand, I didn't see him very much, but you just
know when you're in his presence, you just feel a glow with warmth and love.
And I think too that we were also taught on how to do the right thing as a person.
And I said recently, I said, you know what, he was a genius as a surgeon, but I think
that he was even as great as a person.
Did other athletes on other teams from foreign countries know Dr. Steppen, were they envious

I don't think they're envious, they just flew in and saw him.
I mean, like a Mark Zierdelli, you know, I mean, he had only one World Cup prior to his

And after that injury, I think 40-some wins and one five overall World Cup titles.
But Kobe Bryant, John L. Wade, Dan Marino, obviously from this country, but there were

Andy Mill, one of the best of all time and obviously a great fan of Dr. Richard Steppen.

Olympian Andy Mill speaks to Greg Lewis about Dr. Richard Steadman at the Grateful Steadys event Saturday, December 3rd, 2016.

The Steadman Philippon Research Institute  is dedicated to keeping people of all ages physically active through orthopaedic research and education in the areas of arthritis, healing, rehabilitation, and injury prevention. 

Founded in 1988 by orthopaedic surgeon Dr. J. Richard Steadman, the Steadman Philippon Research Institute is an independent, tax-exempt (IRS code 501(c)(3)) charitable organization, employing scientists, researchers, fellows, visiting scholars, and interns.

The Steadman Philippon Research Institute is known throughout the world for our research into the causes, prevention and treatment of orthopaedic disorders. We are committed to solving orthopaedic problems that limit an individual's ability to maintain an active life.

Our research perspective is based on clinical relevance, with a goal of improving the care of the patient. Recognizing that the body's innate healing powers can be harnessed and manipulated to improve the healing process has led to exciting advances in surgical techniques, such as microfracture and innovative rehabilitation developed by Dr. Richard Steadman, and validated at our Institute. Today, the Institute is recognized worldwide for Dr. Marc Philippon’s pioneering research for the treatment of sports related injuries to the hip.
